transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (SummitStream Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (Eng Mgr), Priya Rao (Data Privacy), Noah Kim (SRE)
Shared materials: SummitStream pilot brief (customer), Redwood pilot deck: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-deck

Summary (auto): Initial scoping for model selection and deployment mode. Focus on large context support and multilingual accuracy. Security/PII gating is primary constraint for private vs hosted decision.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — I'm Maya, account lead at Redwood. Daniel's on for the deep tech — hi Daniel.
[00:00:08] Daniel Ruiz: hey all. ready to nerd out on batching and k v cache stuff.
[00:00:12] Asha Patel: Thanks, Maya. Asha here. I'll kick off with a quick overview of what SummitStream is trying to do, then we can jump into questions.
[00:00:20] Liam O'Connor: Liam here. we'll be responsible for integration.
[00:00:23] Priya Rao: Priya — data privacy. main thing for us is PII handling and key management.
[00:00:27] Noah Kim: Noah, SRE. interested in throughput and latency at scale.
[00:00:31] Maya Chen: Awesome. Asha, over to you.
[00:00:35] Asha Patel: Summarizing quick: we transcribe long-form video to text and then generate chapter summaries, highlight reels and personalized clip recommendations. traffic is global — about 60% en, 25% es, 10% hi/other. latency target is sub-2s for short clip generation paths, and batch jobs can be longer. Current baseline uses an LLM vendor API but cost and context limitations are a problem — we often need entire episode context ~20-30k tokens so we want 16k+ models ideally 32k for some use cases. Also tool-calling to our metadata store and retrieval for grounding.
[00:01:12] Daniel Ruiz: ok that's helpful. quick clarifying — when you say "entire episode" is that full transcript blob per request or do you plan to stream context into the model?
[00:01:22] Asha Patel: We prefer whole blob to keep coherence on long narratives. sometimes we chunk, but for TLDR/chapters want full context.
[00:01:29] Maya Chen: Great. so the model + deployment question breaks down to three axes we usually talk through: model family (open vs closed), context length and ops mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and then tooling like function/tool-calling and retrieval.
[00:01:44] Liam O'Connor: Can you talk a bit about open models — we've been evaluating Mistral and some Llama variants — what are the tradeoffs in quality vs cost?
[00:01:54] Daniel Ruiz: Sure. On open models you get flexibility: you can run on Redwood Hosted for quick testing, Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity with better latency predictability, or Redwood Private if data residency/KMS matters. Mistral and newer Llama forks have good token efficiency, but performance varies on long-context tasks. We recommend testing both 16k and 32k checkpoints. Also some open models have instruction-tuned variants which help summaries.
[00:02:18] Priya Rao: on privacy — hosted is okay if we can guarantee no transcript retention, encryption at rest and key separation. we need SOC2 + audit logs, and ideally CMK / bring-your-own-key.
[00:02:29] Maya Chen: Yep, we can provide SOC2 docs, support KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports customer-managed keys for encryption at rest with additional enterprise contract. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available in Redwood Console. We'll send the security pack after.
[00:02:41] Asha Patel: Great. How about tool-calling? we need the model to call internal APIs (metadata, user prefs) and also do retrieval augmentation.
[00:02:49] Daniel Ruiz: We have function/tool-calling in the hosted API and the runtime supports structured outputs. For private and dedicated you can deploy the same agents; function calling is supported but you should validate latencies — the extra network hop to your internal services can add overhead. Caching and prefix KV cache can help.
[00:03:05] Noah Kim: about that network hop — if we host metadata internally (behind VPC), how does Redwood connect in private mode? we can't have egress to public endpoints for PII.
[00:03:15] Maya Chen: For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) the control plane can be private; you run the runtime in your VPC and we support direct peering or inside-hosted connectors. No egress to public by default; all calls to your metadata stores stay inside network. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[00:03:30] Liam O'Connor: latency wise — what's realistic for a 16k vs 32k context model on Dedicated? we need to plan for spikes during new episode drops.
[00:03:40] Daniel Ruiz: Single-token latency increases with context due to KV cache warmup and attention scaling. On Dedicated with GPUs optimized (A100-class or similar), 16k inference for summarization tasks can often be in 0.8-1.8s range per short clip generation depending on generation length and batch size. 32k will be higher — maybe 1.5-3s for same scenarios. But we can trade cost by using quantized variants and batching. For interactive short clip generation (sub-2s target) we recommend a tuned 16k variant, or a 32k fallback for full-episode jobs.
[00:04:14] Priya Rao: what's the implication for token billing and cost predictability if we do hybrid routing — short paths to hosted small-models and fallbacks to dedicated 32k?
[00:04:24] Maya Chen: You can route by policy — low-latency short paths hit a cost-efficient model, heavy context goes to reserved pool. Redwood Optimize can suggest batch sizes and quantization profiles to reduce unit cost. We'll produce an example costing spreadsheet.
[00:04:38] Asha Patel: On multilingual quality — English and Spanish are core, Hindi is growing. do open models handle that well or do we need finetune/multi-model routing?
[00:04:47] Daniel Ruiz: Some open models are stronger in EN/ES; Hindi support varies. Options: use a single multilingual checkpoint (if available) or router that selects region-specific models per language. We also support light finetuning or retrieval-augmented methods to cover quality gaps. For now we suggest running evals on a sample of your transcripts.
[00:05:05] Noah Kim: service reliability — if Dedicated pool goes down, what's automatic fallback?
[00:05:10] Maya Chen: The smart routing can failover to hosted public pools or lower-latency regional variants. You control fallback policies — e.g., degrade to smaller context model, notify, or queue the request. SLA is included for Dedicated; Private is negotiated.
[00:05:24] Liam O'Connor: any gotchas with function calling and safety? we have to avoid accidental PII leakage when model calls metadata endpoints.
[00:05:32] Priya Rao: exactly — we need strong filters and audit trails for downstream API calls.
[00:05:36] Daniel Ruiz: Best practice: implement a strict shim service in your infra that strictly validates what the model can request, tokenizes or redacts PII before calling internal APIs, and log every request. Redwood Console captures traces and you can forward audit logs to SIEM. We'll share a reference architecture (link: https://redwood.example.com/reference/tool-calling-shim).
[00:05:55] Asha Patel: sounds good. for the pilot, we want you to run three variants: 1) 16k open-model tuned for summaries, 2) 32k open-model for full-episode coherence, 3) small hybrid approach where retrieval provides context windows. include tool-calling enabled tests and multilingual queries.
[00:06:10] Maya Chen: that's a solid plan. Daniel — can you run the pilot config?
[00:06:14] Daniel Ruiz: yep. I'll spin up a benchmark harness. We'll need a sample anonymized dataset and a list of evaluation metrics (ROUGE, qualitative checks, latency P50/P95). Also please indicate which queries must never leave the VPC — for those we can run in Private.
[00:06:28] Asha Patel: we'll send two sets: 1) anonymized public samples, 2) sensitive set we want inside private env.
[00:06:35] Maya Chen: Perfect. we'll propose a hybrid pilot: run non-sensitive samples on Hosted/Dedicated to compare costs and run sensitive set in Private or Dedicated behind VPC depending on your preference.
[00:06:45] Liam O'Connor: estimated timeline for pilot?
[00:06:48] Daniel Ruiz: Once we get the samples, we can kick off bench in ~48 hours for initial results. Full run with multilingual and tool-calling scenarios about one week.
[00:06:56] Priya Rao: What about contractual items — data processing addendum, breach notification SLA?
[00:07:02] Maya Chen: We'll include DPA and standard incident management terms; if you need enhanced breach notification windows we can add that to the enterprise contract.
[00:07:09] Asha Patel: Cost ballpark for Dedicated reserved pool for our expected qps? We're probably looking at bursts of 200-300 concurrent short jobs during peak drops.
[00:07:18] Maya Chen: we'll run sizing with that QPS. Very rough high-level: reserved Dedicated pools reduce per-token cost vs hosted; exact numbers depend on model family, quantization, and regional infra. I'll include a per-variant estimate in the matrix.
[00:07:30] Noah Kim: one more ops question — do you provide kernel-level optimizations or recommendations for GPU type?
[00:07:35] Daniel Ruiz: yes. the runtime picks kernels based on model arch and sequence length distribution. For 32k contexts we often recommend higher memory GPUs (80GB-class like A100 or next-gen variants) or sharded setups; for 16k you can get away with lower memory when using quantization. We'll include a recommended instance matrix.
[00:07:51] Asha Patel: good. any competitors we should be aware of for this tech path?
[00:07:55] Maya Chen: customers often evaluate Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted APIs; for on-prem/inference vendors they'll look at self-hosted runtimes. We position Redwood for predictable economics and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:08:08] Liam O'Connor: ok let's recap next steps quickly.
[00:08:11] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Redwood to send hosted vs dedicated vs private comparison + costing spreadsheet and security pack (SOC2, KMS options) by 2026-03-17; 2) SummitStream to send anonymized sample + sensitive dataset indicator by 2026-03-18; 3) Redwood SE to run 48-hour pilot with three model variants and tool-calling enabled, share results ~2026-03-25; 4) schedule technical deep-dive 2026-03-19 with Noah & Daniel.
[00:08:36] Asha Patel: that works. appreciated.
[00:08:40] Maya Chen: Great. any final quick q's?
[00:08:43] Priya Rao: just confirm audit log retention options.
[00:08:46] Maya Chen: yes, we have configurable retention for logs — we'll include options in the security pack.
[00:08:52] Noah Kim: thanks. I might add a note: we'll want to do a throughput run simulating episode drops during pilot.
[00:08:58] Daniel Ruiz: noted — we'll include a load profile and stress test plan.
[00:09:02] Maya Chen: Perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email with the artifacts and calendar invites.
[00:09:08] Asha Patel: thanks Maya. bye all.
